title: Google Workspace: Docs, Sheets and Slides

videos.script: The same three jobs as the last lesson, and a different idea about where a document is. {{where}} A Word file is an object on a disk that you open, change and save. A Google Doc is something on a server that you look at through a browser, and there is no save because every keystroke has already been sent. {{diff}} That one difference produces everything else: several people in it at once, a history of every version with no effort at all, a link instead of a path, and the awkward fact that you do not hold a copy of it. {{copy}} Which makes sharing the important half of this lesson rather than the features. A link anybody can open is a decision about the whole internet, and the settings that control it are four words with consequences nobody reads. {{share}} We do the three programs, what each has that Office does not, and what breaks when a document crosses between the two. {{cross}} And we finish where lesson eight finished, on the question of what you actually own.
